summary: Practise proposal costing, bargaining briefs, clause drafting, and agreement tracking in five days. Explore the TrainingCred course.
lede: Union relations training covers preparing and administering negotiated employment terms through structured bargaining. It is for labor relations specialists, employee relations managers, union representatives and others who prepare negotiations, represent workforce interests or manage agreements. Participants practise costing proposals in Excel, assessing BATNA and ZOPA bargaining options, and drafting agreement clauses and grievance workflows.
audienceIntro: This collective bargaining course is designed for people who prepare negotiations, represent workforce interests, administer agreements, or advise on their operational effects. This course is designed for: Labor Relations Specialists who prepare employer proposals and bargaining briefs. Union Negotiators who assess proposed collective agreement terms. Employee Relations Managers who oversee negotiations and agreement administration. Collective Bargaining Officers who coordinate mandates and proposal records. Labor Relations Analysts who calculate wage and benefit proposal costs. Union Representatives who present member concerns during bargaining. Workforce Planning Specialists who test proposed staffing and scheduling clauses. Compensation Analysts who model pay-scale changes in negotiated terms. Industrial Relations Directors who report bargaining risks to executive leadership. Employment Counsel who review proposed clauses against applicable requirements.
modules: Collective Bargaining with BATNA and ZOPA
ILO Representative Engagement and Bargaining Scope
prerequisites: Working experience with employee relations, union representation, workforce policy, or negotiated employment terms is expected. Familiarity with basic spreadsheet formulas helps with proposal costing; coding is not required. Advanced legal interpretation and production automation are outside the applied exercises.
